raw.help:
FACILITY SYSTEM GUIDE
====================

Facilities are station-based structures you build, own, and operate. You must be docked to interact with them.

FACILITY CATEGORIES
-------------------
- production: Automated crafting. Runs the crafting jobs queued on it, pulling inputs from storage and depositing outputs back to storage. Built by a player ('build') or directly by a faction ('faction_build'); player- or faction-owned.
- faction: Shared faction infrastructure (storage, crafting, trading, intel, recruitment, rooms, missions). Always on. Requires ManageFacilities faction permission to build/upgrade.
- personal: Player home and passive bonuses. Personal Quarters sets your home station (respawn point). Trader's Office gives a market fee discount and Drone Control adds drone bandwidth. The Workshop's crafting bonus is not currently applied.
- service: Station-owned (market, repair, refueling, shipyard). Not player-buildable.
- infrastructure: Station-owned power and life support. Not player-buildable.

HOW PRODUCTION WORKS
--------------------
Production facilities run a queue of crafting jobs. Add work with the 'craft'/'recycle' commands (which auto-route a job to a facility that can run it) or with 'job_add' directly; station-owned facilities are fed automatically by the station manager.

Work runs continuously over ticks, not in fixed cycles: each tick a facility spends one unit of production budget advancing its queue, and a run completes once its crafting time accumulates. Output is deposited to storage as each run finishes (you get a 'crafting_update' notification). Inputs and labor are escrowed up front when the job is queued and consumed run by run (refunded if you cancel).

Throughput scales with TIER, not output size: each tier is ~3x faster than the one below (T1 1x, T2 3x, T3 9x, T4 27x). Higher tiers make the same items, just faster — upgrading never increases the quantity per run.

Player-owned facilities pull inputs from / deposit outputs to your personal station storage. Faction-owned facilities use faction storage and bill production labor to the faction treasury per run.

A facility makes no progress on a tick if: it has no queued work, is under construction, is missing inputs in storage, or the owner can't cover the per-run labor cost. Power matters too — if the facilities crafting at a station draw more power than supply plus stored battery, every facility there is throttled proportionally.

PACKAGE LOGISTICS
-----------------
Logistics facilities run the same crafting queue and rental system. job_add with recipe_id="pack_package" takes items=[{item_id,quantity}, ...], label, source, and target. job_add with recipe_id="unpack_package" takes package_id, source, and target. source/target accept storage, cargo, faction, or faction:<bucket>; target defaults to source. Packing consumes one cargo_container. Logistics unpacking returns it.

Logistics rental pricing is charged once per package operation: one pack or one unpack job pays the configured price once, regardless of manifest size. Ordinary production remains priced per produced unit.

RENT & MAINTENANCE
------------------
Player-owned facilities (production and personal) and faction-owned tenant facilities pay rent every maintenance cycle (100 ticks / ~17 minutes). A personal facility pays a flat rent by level: 1,000 / 2,500 / 5,000 / 10,000 credits per day for levels 1-4. Every other facility pays 3% of its build cost per day. Pirate stations charge double. A facility cycle is 1/86 of a day, so rent_per_cycle is the daily rent divided by 86. A rent cut applies at once; a rent rise is capped at 50% per day.

- Personal rent is auto-deducted from your credit wallet (wherever you are); faction rent is paid from the faction treasury. Rent goes to the station manager, or to the owning faction's treasury at a player-built faction station or outpost.
- If the wallet or treasury can't cover rent, the unpaid cycles accrue as ARREARS and are charged once that payer can cover them.
- A facility with arrears stays yours, but it STOPS WORKING until the arrears are paid: no production, services, or bonuses. Storage, fuel bunkers, and ship garages keep working, so you can always reach your goods. You cannot transfer or sell a facility while it owes rent. You get a warning at the first missed cycle and once a day after that.
- An inactive owner (no gameplay this weekly tax period) accrues no new arrears. A faction accrues none while no member is active.
- Idle but usable facilities still pay rent; rent is paused during construction, while damaged or repairing, and while dismantling. Existing arrears are preserved, not forgiven, and missed-rent cycles do not advance during the pause. A listed rent_per_cycle is the stored rate, not a charge while paused; rent totals include only currently chargeable facilities.
- maintenance_per_cycle is a facility's listed upkeep, not what it burns each cycle. A facility needs on hand only what it draws that cycle (maintenance_average_burn_per_cycle on average), so a few units at a time keep it running. If a draw fails the facility goes offline, and it comes back at the next cycle once at least one of each upkeep item is in storage. Dining/leisure venues (tourism_upkeep) are the exception: they eat only what their paying guests order, so a busy one burns about its whole listed stock each cycle and an empty one burns none — restock busy venues every cycle.
- A faction's facilities at its own station or outpost are rent-free, and so are its members' personal facilities there. Any other owner there is a tenant and pays rent to the owning faction's treasury, with the same arrears rules. Faction tenant facilities at other stations pay rent.

Tip: Use action 'owned' or 'faction_owned' to see the rent bill across all stations. Keep enough credits in the relevant wallet or treasury.

CONSTRUCTION
------------
Building or upgrading a facility starts construction. The facility is not operational until construction completes.

- Build time varies by type and tier (1 tick = 10 seconds). A Crew Bunk takes ~100s; a Faction Stronghold takes ~67 minutes.
- Cost: credits from your wallet + materials from your cargo and/or station storage.
- Optionally pass package_ids (an array) on 'build'/'faction_build' to source materials directly from those packages instead of unpacking them into storage first — see DISMANTLE & MOVING FACILITIES.
- Skill gate: tier 2+ facilities require Corporation Management skill at the facility's level.
- Check progress with 'list' or 'faction_list'.

UPGRADES
--------
Facilities can be upgraded to higher tiers for improved throughput, capacity, or bonuses.

- Upgrading REPLACES the old facility. A new one is created and starts under construction.
- Use action 'upgrades' to see available upgrade paths at your current station.
- Each tier has its own credit and material costs. Optionally pass package_ids on 'upgrade'/'faction_upgrade' the same way as 'build'.

DISMANTLE & MOVING FACILITIES
-----------------------------
You can dismantle a facility into ordinary labeled packages containing every material used to build its full upgrade chain.

- 'dismantle' (facility_id) for a facility you own; 'faction_dismantle' for a faction facility (requires ManageFacilities).
- Dismantling takes the cumulative build and upgrade time, finishing on the next station maintenance cycle after that. The facility goes offline immediately and is removed when the timer completes, when the packages appear in personal or faction storage here. The ticks_to_complete and complete_tick in the response already account for this.
- Dismantling costs one cargo_container per package produced — have enough on hand in storage (or faction storage) before dismantling, or it's rejected up front.
- Each tier of the facility's upgrade chain is packaged separately (the base tier's materials, then each upgrade tier's), so you can rebuild in stages from the matching tier's packages instead of one giant mixed pile. Each package occupies 100 cargo and holds up to 100 unpacked cargo size, so a tier's materials may still span multiple numbered packages.
- Packages use the normal package system: move, trade, gift, and inspect them normally.
- To rebuild: either unpack them normally and use the recovered materials, OR pass their package_ids straight to 'build'/'upgrade' (or the faction equivalents) to source materials directly from them — no separate unpack step, and each consumed package's cargo_container comes back. Packages are consumed whole, so each one must contain exactly what that build/upgrade still needs of an item — no more — or the whole action is rejected before anything is touched; materials a package doesn't cover can still come from storage or cargo as usual. Credits and skills are still required.
- The full material set is returned; credits are not refunded.
- Damaged facilities can be dismantled without repairing them first. Starting dismantling cancels any in-progress repair; repair costs already spent are not refunded.
- You can't dismantle a facility under construction or already dismantling, one listed for sale, or one with queued production jobs. Personal Quarters can be dismantled after your other personal facilities here are gone; Faction Storage after your faction's other facilities here are gone, including ones still dismantling. Removing quarters does not change your home base.
- Remaining faction items and dismantling packages stay available to view and withdraw with the usual permissions, but new deposits stop when storage dismantling starts unless your faction owns the station (which grants storage independently). An outpost's built-in storage and fuel bunker require dismantle_outpost instead.

FACILITY EXCHANGE (SELLING)
---------------------------
Production facilities you no longer need can be listed for sale to other players or the station manager.

- 'list_for_sale' with facility_id and price puts a player-owned facility up for sale. Add "faction": true to list a faction-owned facility (requires ManageFacilities). Listing fee is 1% of price (non-refundable).
- The facility KEEPS RUNNING while listed — output and rent still accrue to the current owner until it sells.
- 'browse_for_sale' shows listings at your current station (filter by max_price or facility_type).
- 'buy_listing' with listing_id transfers ownership and pays the seller. Sales tax applies.
- 'cancel_listing' with listing_id removes a listing you posted (fee not refunded).
- Station managers may buy listed facilities themselves during their build-or-buy evaluation — if a listing matches an empty production niche, they prefer buying over building fresh.

TRANSFERS
---------
Production facilities can be transferred between personal and faction ownership. Only production facilities — not faction services or personal facilities. To start a production facility under faction ownership from scratch, use 'faction_build' directly — transfer is for handing over a facility that already exists.

To faction (direction="to_faction"):
  - You must own the facility.
  - Your faction must have Faction Storage at that station.
  - Effect: facility becomes faction-owned, inputs/outputs switch to faction storage, and the faction treasury pays tenant rent (rent-free if the faction owns this station).

To player (direction="to_player"):
  - Requires ManageFacilities permission.
  - Target player must be in the same faction and docked at the same station.
  - Omit player_id to transfer to yourself.
  - Effect: facility becomes player-owned, inputs/outputs switch to player storage, and the player's wallet pays rent, subject to the same lifecycle pauses.

FACTION FACILITIES
------------------
Faction facilities unlock shared features at a station. Faction Storage must be built FIRST — it gates all other faction facilities. One per service type per faction per station. Requires ManageFacilities permission.

- faction_storage (Lockbox > Warehouse > Depot > Stronghold): Shared item/credit vault. Capacity per item: 100k/200k/300k/500k by tier.
- faction_admin (Desk > Office): Gates faction customization and settings.
- faction_recruitment (Hiring Board > Desk > Center > Guild Hall > Grand Bureau): Member cap: 50/100/200/400/1000 by tier.
- faction_market (Market Runner > Trading Booth > Trading Post): Faction exchange orders. Order cap: 100/250/500 by tier.
- faction_commons (Quarters > Lounge > Clubhouse): Faction rooms for player-written content. Room cap: 1/3/6 by tier.
- faction_missions (Notice Board > Mission Board > Bounty Office): Faction-posted missions. Cap: 3/8/15 by tier.
- faction_intel (Intel Terminal > Intel Center): Shared exploration data. L1 = manual submission, L2 = automatic when members visit systems.
- faction_trade_intel (Trade Ledger > Commerce Terminal): Shared market prices. L1 = manual, L2 = auto-collects when members dock.

WILDLIFE RANCHES
----------------
A ranch (Wildlife Corral > Range Station > Ranch Complex) is a faction facility built on a FACTION OUTPOST whose anchor POI is a habitat of the grazer you want to ranch. Build with faction_build, facility_type=wildlife_corral, species=<species id> — the species is fixed for the facility's life. Requires Xenobiology (8/12/16 by tier), a domesticable grazer (not every grazer can be ranched), and a live wild population in the system (survey_system shows the census).

How it runs, every facility cycle (~17 min), all from faction storage at the outpost:
- WORKER SUPPLIES (oxygen, water, fuel cells + labor credits): all-or-nothing. Unsupplied, the whole ranch stalls and the herd drifts back to the wild.
- FEED: the species' diet resource, in proportion to the herd. Partial feed = partial herd; unfed animals starve and rewild. Mining feed at the anchor POI is self-defeating — un-mined diet nodes set your capacity ("range health") and feed the wild pool you domesticate from.
- OUTPUTS: fed herds trickle their diet-yield secretions live, plus any husbandry products the species gives (milk, eggs — RANCH-ONLY: no kill, wild or branded, ever drops them). 'ranch_set_cull' (cull_target=N) slaughters surplus above N each cycle for the full loot table. Sustainable cull ≈ the growth rate shown in ranch_status.
- DOMESTICATION: wild animals join a supplied, fed ranch over time — but never below a wild reserve. Protect your wild pool; it is your breeding stock.

Branded ranch animals stand at the anchor POI and are huntable by ANYONE — lawless space has no crime. get_nearby, scan, and survey_system show the brand, branded kills earn no hunt mission credit, and your faction is notified exactly who pulled the trigger. Defense is your problem: park a cruiser next to it or make friends with the neighbors.

Use 'ranch_status' (docked at the outpost, or facility_id=...) for the full readout.

PERSONAL FACILITIES
-------------------
Personal facilities provide a home base and passive bonuses. Personal Quarters must be built FIRST — it gates all others. One per service type per player per station.

- quarters (Crew Bunk > Private Cabin > Officer's Suite > Captain's Estate): Home station / respawn point. Customizable description, public or private access.
- workshop (Workshop Toolkit > Workshop Power Tools > Workshop Fabricator): Speeds up your hand-crafting at the Station Workshop, at the station where it's built (+5%/10%/15% workshop speed).
- drone_control (Signal Relay > Control Hub > Command Center): Adds drone bandwidth (lets you run more drones at once).
- trader_office (Ledger Desk > Trading Office > Brokerage): Market fee discount: 25%/50%/75% off exchange listing fees.

ACTIONS REFERENCE
-----------------
Browse & Info:
  types                             — Browse facility types. Params: facility_type, category, name, level, page, per_page.
  list                              — View all facilities at current station: yours, your faction's, station services, plus public facilities others (players or factions) rent out here — with each one's per-run rental price.
  owned                             — View ALL facilities you own across every station, with your total rent bill per cycle and per day.
  faction_list                      — View your faction's facilities at current station.
  faction_owned                     — View ALL facilities your faction owns across every station, with labor costs.
  upgrades                          — View available upgrades for your facilities here.

Building:
  build(facility_type)              — Build a player-owned production facility. Credits from wallet, materials from cargo/storage.
  faction_build(facility_type)      — Build a faction facility OR a faction-owned production facility directly. Faction Storage (faction_lockbox) must exist first. Credits/materials from faction treasury then your wallet. Requires ManageFacilities.
  personal_build(facility_type)     — Build a personal facility. Quarters (crew_bunk) must exist first.

Upgrading:
  upgrade(facility_id, facility_type)         — Upgrade a player-owned facility to a higher tier.
  faction_upgrade(facility_id, facility_type)  — Upgrade a faction facility. Requires ManageFacilities.

Dismantle & Move:
  dismantle(facility_id)            — Package 100% of cumulative build and upgrade materials after the cumulative build time (finishing on the next station maintenance cycle). Unpack at the destination and rebuild normally.
  faction_dismantle(facility_id)    — Same for a faction facility. Requires ManageFacilities; packages go to faction storage. A ship garage must be emptied first.

Repair (after a station has been shot up):
  repair(facility_id)               — Put a damaged facility back. A station that loses a fight is wrecked, not destroyed: it keeps its market and storage, loses everything else, and every facility on it is left damaged. Repair costs 30% of the facility's original build materials and 30% of its build time (finishing on the next station maintenance cycle). Use 'list' to see which are damaged; the station comes back online once they are repaired.

Faction Ship Garage (shared fleet pool):
  Build the garage with faction_build facility_type=faction_ship_garage (holds 20; upgrade to faction_ship_hangar=50, faction_fleet_yard=100). It is then used through the normal ship commands — no garage-specific actions:
    • Store a ship: gift it to your faction — send_gift recipient=faction ship_id=<id> (or storage action=deposit target=faction item_id=<ship_id>). The ship must be parked here and not your active ship.
    • Take a ship out: switch_ship ship_id=<id> while docked here — switching to a pooled ship claims it (ownership transfers to you) and flies it.
    • See what's pooled: list_ships shows the faction garage at your current station.

Transfer:
  transfer(facility_id, direction)  — Transfer production facility. direction="to_faction" or "to_player". Optional: player_id (for to_player).

Exchange (sales):
  list_for_sale(facility_id, price)         — List a production facility for sale. Add "faction": true to list a faction-owned facility.
  browse_for_sale()                         — Browse facility listings at the current station. Optional filters: max_price, facility_type.
  buy_listing(listing_id)                   — Buy a listed facility. Ownership transfers to you and rent starts from your wallet.
  cancel_listing(listing_id)                — Remove your own (or your faction's) listing. Fee not refunded.

Personal Quarters:
  personal_decorate(description, access) — Write quarters description (max 4000 chars). access="public" or "private".
  personal_visit(username)               — Visit quarters. Omit username for your own.

Naming & Description:
  set_name(facility_id, custom_name)     — Give a facility you own a custom name (3-32 chars) so multiple facilities of the same type stand out in 'list'/'owned'. Send an empty custom_name to clear it.
  set_description(facility_id, description) — Give a facility you own a custom description (max 4000 chars), overriding its default flavor text in 'list'. Works on any owned facility — e.g. re-flavor your faction's bar. Send an empty description to clear it.

TIPS
----
- Use types with category="production" or category="faction" to browse buildable facility types.
- Queue work with craft/job_add and keep inputs stocked in storage; station-owned facilities are auto-fed by the station manager.
- Transfer production facilities to your faction to eliminate rent and use shared storage.
- Higher tiers run faster (~3x per tier) — same output per run, not more — and cost more to build and maintain.
- Check action 'owned' regularly — rent drains your wallet from every station at once, and a facility with unpaid arrears stops working until you pay them.
